$comment: Facet personalisation settings (single source for the WASM renderer; copied 2026-10-22 from Facet main packages/settings/src/settings.json, accent colours left out: they live in tokens/colour.json accents, the generator checks the ids). tools/gen_settings.mjs -> settings_gen.h (fw::set::) -> screens/settings.cpp. Same schema later feeds the panel's Home Assistant entities and the ESPHome web page. Facet personalisation settings: the one schema behind the on-panel Settings screen, the panel's Home Assistant entities (ESPHome template selects/numbers/switches), the ESPHome web_server page and the docs playground controls. Option labels are the exact option strings Home Assistant shows. esphome.id keeps the firmware's existing entity ids so Home Assistant entity ids never change.

settings.help: Whether the panel is light or dark. Auto is light while the sun is up and dark after sunset.
settings.label: Mode

options.label: Auto
options.hint: light while the sun is up

settings.help: The panel's theme: Facet, a theme built into the panel, or the one Home Assistant sent (facet_theme). A theme the panel refuses is never shown: Facet stays.
settings.label: Theme
settings.about: Themes change the look only (colours, faces, edges, shapes); sizes, layout and touch targets stay Facet's. Every theme passes the same guards as Facet: structure, ranges, contrast in every mode and accent, press feedback.

settings.help: The one colour used for what matters, such as what is playing or what needs you. current keeps the colour in use now.
settings.label: Accent
settings.about: The one colour for what matters: playing, needs you, the hero ring. Every set passes contrast in both themes: fill 3:1 against the canvas and cards, accent text 4.5:1, label on accent 4.5:1.

settings.help: How big the small text is. Large makes small text one step bigger without moving anything on the screen.
settings.label: Text size
settings.about: Large sets the small text roles one step bigger inside the same line boxes, so nothing on a screen moves (480: titles only; body and label line boxes have no room there).

settings.help: Turns the picture to match how the panel is mounted. Touch turns with it.
settings.label: Rotate screen
settings.about: Clockwise, applied at once without a restart (panel firmware: LVGL rotation, the touch points turn with it). The workbench and docs previews stay upright.

settings.help: Turns the panel's taps and alert sounds on or off.
settings.label: UI sounds

settings.help: Which set of sounds the panel plays, each with its own character, from soft keycaps to playful arcade blips.
settings.label: Sound pack

settings.help: How loud the panel's sounds are, from 0 (silent) to 100.
settings.label: Volume

settings.help: How many seconds with no touch before the panel shows the clock. 0 never goes idle.
settings.label: Clock after
settings.about: No touch for this long: the clock shows, without its header. A touch goes back to Home.

settings.help: How bright the screen is while the idle clock shows, from 10 to 100 percent.
settings.label: Idle brightness

settings.help: How many minutes with no touch before the screen turns off, counted from the last touch (the idle clock does not restart it). 0 keeps it on.
settings.label: Screen off after

settings.help: How a new screen appears: instant shows it at once; rise fades its rows in from below.
settings.label: Transition
settings.about: Content rise fades each new screen's rows in. Boards that can't keep up default to Instant.

settings.help: Which firmware updates the panel offers: Stable releases, or Beta builds that come more often and may have rough edges.
settings.label: Update channel
settings.about: Picks the update manifest the panel's Firmware entity checks (ota.json or ota-beta.json beside it). Switching back to Stable offers the stable build, even when it is older. The workbench and docs ignore it.

settings.help: Where messages such as a finished timer appear: at the top or the bottom of the screen.
settings.label: Toast position

settings.help: Whether every distance on the panel, such as aircraft overhead or the nearest lightning, is shown in kilometres or miles.
settings.label: Distance
settings.about: Every distance a screen shows: aircraft overhead, the nearest lightning strike, the Overhead and Lightning radar rings.

settings.help: How every speed on the panel, such as wind or aircraft, is shown: miles per hour, kilometres per hour, or knots.
settings.label: Speed
settings.about: Every speed a screen shows: aircraft overhead, wind, a storm's approach.

settings.help: Lets scripts, automations and agents on your network change this panel. Each one asks for its own key, and you tap Allow on the panel. Off: every key is refused. Turn it on here, in the panel's editor or in Home Assistant.
settings.label: Allow API access
settings.about: Off: every write from outside the panel's own editor is refused, keys too, and no key can be asked for. On: a request with Authorization: Bearer <key> (a key from POST /fw/keys/request, allowed on the glass) can do what the editor does. Reads, /llms.txt, /agents.md, /ai and /schema.json are always open.
